foundation.work: Watch whether the child counts on from 14 or restarts from 1.
Ask how they know. Common error: choosing the number said first.

foundation.q: I have 6 sweets. I get 3 more. How many sweets now?
foundation.work: Watch for counting on fingers or objects (fine) versus guessing.
Accept 'triangle'. Note if the child confuses it with a square or says 'pyramid'.

core.q: What number goes with 7 to make 10?
core.work: Does the child know the bond, or count up from 7 on fingers?

core.q: Here is a pattern: 5, 10, 15, then what comes next?
core.work: Look for counting in 5s. Common error: 16 (adding 1) or 25.

core.q: A pencil costs 40 cents. An eraser costs 30 cents. How much for both?
core.work: Watch tens-and-ones thinking (4 tens + 3 tens). Common error: 7 cents or 10 cents.

core.q: 5 children like apples. 3 like bananas. 2 like grapes. How many more like apples than grapes?
core.work: Common error: adding (7) or giving the apple count (5) instead of comparing.

core.q: A pen is 8 cubes long. A ruler is 12 cubes long. How many cubes longer is the ruler?
core.work: Does the child compare (12 - 8) or add? Ask them to show with fingers or cubes.

core.q: Ali is taller than Ben. Ben is taller than Cai. Who is the shortest?
core.work: Ask the child to line them up. Common error: answering Ben or Ali.

stretch.q: Two numbers add up to 10. One is 4 more than the other. What are the two numbers?
stretch.work: Look for trial and error with bonds to 10 (good). Common error: 4 and 6, which only differ by 2.

stretch.q: I have 5 coins. Some are 10-cent coins and some are 5-cent coins. Together they make 40 cents. How many of each?
stretch.work: Look for guess-and-check. Common error: 4 and 1, which has the right count but makes 45 cents.
